name: Tail of the Dragon · US 129
description: 318 curves in 11 miles of US 129 between Deals Gap, on the North Carolina–Tennessee line, and Chilhowee Lake in Tennessee. No intersections, driveways or side roads along the way, and no guardrail for much of it.

sources.title: US129DragonsTail.com: Tail of the Dragon overview

speed.note: OpenStreetMap tags most of the Tennessee side at 30 mph, but this project does not treat OSM tags alone as a verified source. Follow posted signs.

access.note: US 129 is currently carrying detour traffic from I-40 repairs near the state line (Hurricane Helene damage), and TDOT/NCDOT enforce a strict length limit on this stretch as a result: no truck-trailer combinations or single units over 30 ft. Check current conditions before a trip.

name: Cherohala Skyway
description: A 43-mile National Scenic Byway between Tellico Plains, Tennessee, and Robbinsville, North Carolina, climbing to 5,390 ft. Long, sweeping mountain curves rather than tight hairpins — a different character from the Dragon it connects to at the Robbinsville end.

sources.title: National Scenic Byway Foundation: Cherohala Skyway

speed.note: OpenStreetMap tags parts of the North Carolina side at 45 mph, but this project does not treat OSM tags alone as a verified source. Follow posted signs.

access.note: Closes unpredictably above about 4,000 ft in icy or snowy conditions, typically November through March, sometimes with little notice. North Carolina plows its side; Tennessee's side does not get plowed the same way. Check current status before a winter or early-spring trip.

name: Back of the Dragon · VA 16
description: 32 miles of Virginia Route 16 between Marion and Tazewell, Virginia, crossing Clinch Mountain with more than 400 curves — Virginia's officially designated motorcycle route, and the Dragon's sister road in the Southern Appalachians touge circuit.

sources.title: Back of the Dragon: the official route site

speed.note: OpenStreetMap tags this route between 25 and 55 mph depending on the section (town centers vs. open highway), but this project does not treat OSM tags alone as a verified source. Follow posted signs.

access.note: Check current Virginia road conditions before a trip; mountain sections can ice over in winter.

name: Devil's Whip · NC 80
area: Blue Ridge Parkway corridor, North Carolina
description: 12 miles of North Carolina Highway 80 between Buck Creek Gap on the Blue Ridge Parkway and Marion, NC, with around 160 curves and roughly 2,000 ft of elevation change along Buck Creek.

sources.title: Motorcycle Roads: North Carolina's Route 80 (Devil's Whip)

speed.note: OpenStreetMap tags this route between 35 and 55 mph depending on the section, but this project does not treat OSM tags alone as a verified source. Follow posted signs.

access.note: This road has real closure history: a mudslide shut part of it in 2018, and a nearby wildfire closed a section as recently as March 2026. It also crosses the Blue Ridge Parkway at Buck Creek Gap, which has its own seasonal and weather closures. Check DriveNC.gov before a trip.

name: Wolf Pen Gap Road · GA 180
description: The 11-mile western section of Georgia Highway 180 between Suches and the US 19/129 concurrency, a favorite of the North Georgia riding community. The road continues east as a separate named section (Bald Mountain Road) after the concurrency, not mapped here.

sources.title: Motorcycle Cruiser: Georgia's State Route 180, Wolf Pen Gap Road

speed.note: OpenStreetMap tags this section at 35 mph, but this project does not treat OSM tags alone as a verified source. Follow posted signs.

access.note: Check current Georgia road conditions before a trip; mountain sections can ice over in winter.

name: Richard B. Russell Scenic Highway · GA 348
description: 14 miles of Georgia Highway 348 through the Chattahoochee National Forest between Helen and Blairsville, on the eastern side of the Russell–Brasstown Scenic Byway. Rolling mountain curves rather than tight switchbacks.

sources.title: Now Habersham: GA 348 winter closure notice

speed.note: OpenStreetMap tags this route at 30 mph, but this project does not treat OSM tags alone as a verified source. Follow posted signs.

access.note: Georgia DOT closes this road as a precaution ahead of snow, ice or freezing rain — a routine practice here, not a rare event. Check current Georgia road conditions before a winter trip.
